artifacts.summary: Recommends a sha256 description-fingerprint field on new .decisions.json entries, compared at dispatch-render time to mark a Prior Decision POTENTIALLY SUPERSEDED when the task description has changed since it was recorded, rejecting last_updated (too noisy) and inline dated-marker text parsing (unschemed, single occurrence) as the detection signal.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system codebase, state.json's per-task last_updated is bumped by many writers unrelated to the task description (dispatch_seq_counter, pending_dispatch, cycle_count, infra_failures writes in skill-base.sh, orchestrate-loop-guard-init.sh, orchestrate-stage5-gates.sh). It is too noisy to use as a proxy for 'has the description changed' -- use a content fingerprint (sha256) of the specific field instead.

This codebase has an established degrade idiom for content fingerprinting: sha256sum with `command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2` (or equivalent), omitting the hash field entirely (never an empty-string placeholder) when the tool is unavailable. Seen in scripts/lib/deploy-ledger-lib.sh and orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's identical-dispatch convergence guard. Reuse this idiom rather than inventing a new one when adding any new content-fingerprint field.
